key_idea: Reduce Euclidean Ramsey-ness to the solvability of an exact rational tensor equation over the coordinate field. Realize solutions via a Laurent-polynomial and lattice identity, built with formal logarithms and flatness of completion, which yields two-scale coordinate-permutation configurations. Then convert these into monochromatic copies using ultrafilter semigroups and Hales–Jewett.
reason: Several individual steps are striking and clean. These include the descent from R⊗R to B, the flatness-of-completion trick that turns a quadratic tensor condition into a finite lattice identity, the PSD padding that produces exact two-scale configurations, and the one-line proof of sphericity. However, the full argument is a long chain of heterogeneous machinery (commutative algebra, smoothing functions, ultrafilters, Hales–Jewett, cost bookkeeping in groups), and it is hard to hold in your head at once. The core reason the criterion is right becomes visible, but it is spread across many verifying lemmas, so the proof reads as a powerful technical achievement more than a book proof.
